lastText: File ClosedThe Wall Paid For in ShellsContestedSoviet High Command, 1941 — 1945End of hostilities: NOVEMBER 1945 (PROJECTED) — filed late, out of sequenceImmediate AftermathVictory in Europe arrives around November 1945 — later than the historical May 1945, the price of choices that spent time to save men. The army that reaches Berlin has paid for the ground twice over — a war fought closer to the historical pattern of holding rigid lines regardless of the arithmetic, at the cost this campaign keeps returning to. The industrial evacuation was subordinated to front supply in 1941 — easing that autumn's crisis at a cost in Urals production capacity that every later year of this campaign quietly pays for. The autumn 1942 reserve was weighted entirely south — Mars never launched, the Rzhev grinder's cost declined, and the single-theater concentration tested against the pinning argument Mars's defenders always made. An early, aggressive evacuation across Lake Ladoga was prioritized over holding the city rigidly — no version of the siege escapes its catastrophe, but this path distributes it differently. Germany's defeat was not a variable Soviet command decisions controlled, only its timing and its price.One Year LaterVictory arrived behind the historical May 1945, which means Soviet forces are still consolidating a front the historical record had a year's head start settling by this point.
